source.title: MoralSteer: Safety-Preserving Fidelity Gains in Morally Complex Role-Playing via Theory-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation
source.authors: Shao-Jie Shi; Te-Qi Hao; Bo-Hao Lv; Rui Xu; Zheng-Yu Shi; Ying-Hui Xu

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates safety behavior after role-play training in a new setting, including benchmark rates and MFT-framed attacks. It does not test the specific data sizes, data types, or token-localization mechanisms in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper measures safety outcomes after role-play training, which is related to the claim’s subject, but its training data and interventions do not match the specific versions. Role-play fidelity scores and personality-expression scores are not harmful-compliance measures. The reported per-token KL is a training objective, not a measurement of aligned-versus-base KL across response positions. MFT-framed persona attacks are not tests of compliant-token prefilling, suffixes, or decoding changes.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes safety-aligned instruct models on non-harmful (morally dark fictional role-play) data and measures harmful compliance against the aligned base. It runs two recipes. Naive SFT on L3/L4 role-play data raises HarmBench ASR (0.138 to 0.226 at Qwen3.5-9B scale) and lowers composite safety. MoralSteer on-policy self-distillation, anchored to the frozen aligned teacher, keeps benchmark safety within ±1pp and lowers HarmBench ASR. Both bear on V2 in a new setting, role-play fine-tuning. Nothing bears on V1 or V3 to V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Add that the authors present Naive FT on L3/L4 role-play data as a safety-regression control that gains fidelity but loses safety (ASR 0.226, composite 0.659). They claim MoralSteer avoids this while improving villain fidelity +5.8 to +9.9%.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses about 120k role-play training examples and theory-guided on-policy self-distillation with privileged MFT chains; it does not use few-shot harmful or ordinary benign instruction fine-tuning to test safety erosion, nor measure response-position KL concentration.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported safety outcomes vary across benchmarks and model families; MFT-framed attack ASR varies with framing strength. The strongest scaffold yields 29/80 versus 52/80, while the plain harmful-request condition is 0.0% for both listed systems.

fits_no_version.finding: Persona and MFT-structured framing raises harmful ASR of the aligned Qwen3.5-9B from 0% to 65% (fictional-scene scaffold).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Role-play persona scaffolds bypass refusal in aligned models (prompt-level jailbreak, not opening-token manipulation).

fits_no_version.finding: Over-refusal on XSTest safe prompts is unchanged (±0.6pp) after MoralSteer training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety-anchored role-play distillation does not change over-refusal.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: Safety-battery point estimates have no reported uncertainty intervals in the table. The paper notes that its judge is primarily GPT-5.5, experiments cover models up to 9B, and its benchmark results do not guarantee safety under stronger or unseen adaptive attacks. The naive fine-tuning ASR row does not clearly identify its matched checkpoint.
record.rows_left_out: Role-play fidelity, personality, MFT-dimension ablations, and training-loss results were not included because they do not directly measure harmful compliance or the response-position mechanisms in the claim.

untested.parts: Ordinary instruction data (e.g. Alpaca/Dolly), carefully selected benign data, dose and data-size effects, and closed models are untested. Only role-play fiction data is used.
No aligned-vs-base per-token KL by response position. The per-token KL in the paper is a training loss.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks. Persona framings are prompt-level jailbreaks.
No analysis of why alignment is shallow.

missing.what: HarmBench ASR base vs MoralSteer for all four bases: 0.138→0.082, 0.134→0.089, 0.409→0.221, 0.159→0.094.
Human safety annotation: harm-boundary crossings 0/300 MoralSteer, 0/300 base, 9/300 Naive FT.
Ablated MoralSteer variants' HarmBench ASR; some exceed base 0.138 (only-FKL 0.176, w/o SFT warmup 0.126 vs full 0.082). Recipe choices matter for erosion.
Same-data SFT/DPO/OPD-without-MFT variants have ASR 0.108–0.116, all below base 0.138, at Qwen3.5-9B scale.

record.verdict_notes: Whether villain role-play fiction counts as 'benign' data for V2 is debatable. It contains no harmful-request completions, but it is deliberately dark, so V2 support is in a new setting. MoralSteer is effectively a safety-preserving recipe (KL to the frozen aligned teacher, refusal-rollout filtering), so its no-erosion result reflects design. The Naive FT base model is identified only through the Table 3 caption ('Qwen3.5-9B scale'). The judge is GPT-5.5. There are no CIs on the safety battery.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fine-tune on a few to a few hundred harmful examples; its role-play training data and safety comparisons do not test that intervention.
Does not test ordinary or carefully chosen benign instruction data as the fine-tuning intervention.
Does not measure per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions.
Does not test compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as ways to bypass refusal.
Does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Does not test whether training data or the training objective causes first-token shallowness.
Does not train or evaluate safety training designed to spread behavior beyond the first response tokens.

relationships.condition: Naive SFT on L3/L4 villain role-play data, Qwen3.5-9B scale
relationships.reason: HarmBench ASR rises 0.138 to 0.226 and composite safety falls 0.787 to 0.659 (R27, R28). Naive FT also has 9/300 harm-boundary crossings vs 0/300 for base (text, Sec 4.6).
relationships.display_finding: HarmBench attack success rose from 0.138 to 0.226 and composite safety fell from 0.787 to 0.659. The naively tuned model also crossed harm boundaries in 9 of 300 cases versus 0 of 300 for the base.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Naive SFT on L3/L4 villain role-play data, Qwen3.5-9B scale
source_check.reason: R27–R28 show safety erosion: composite safety 0.787 → 0.659 and HarmBench ASR 0.138 → 0.226 with corrected baselines. Human annotation also finds 9/300 harm-boundary crossings versus 0/300 for the base.

relationships.condition: MoralSteer on-policy self-distillation from the frozen aligned teacher on the same role-play data, four 3B–9B bases
relationships.reason: Safety rates stay within ±1pp on five benchmarks (R01–R23), composite safety rises (R25, R26), and attack ASR is equal or lower (R30–R36). Erosion depends on the training recipe. Table 1 also shows HarmBench ASR falling on all four bases (text).
relationships.display_finding: Safety rates stayed within ±1 pp on five benchmarks, composite safety rose, and HarmBench ASR fell on all four bases, so erosion depended on the training recipe.
